"""Boundary models for the foundational non-absorbing Phase 1 surface."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import Field, field_validator, model_validator

from autofdtd.core.models import TaggedModel


def _normalize_optional_name(value: str | None) -> str | None:
    if value is None:
        return None
    stripped = value.strip()
    if not stripped:
        raise ValueError("names must not be empty or whitespace-only")
    return stripped


class BoundaryEdge(TaggedModel):
    """Base model for one simulation-domain boundary edge."""

    name: str | None = None

    @field_validator("name")
    @classmethod
    def _validate_name(cls, value: str | None) -> str | None:
        return _normalize_optional_name(value)


class Periodic(BoundaryEdge):
    """Periodic boundary condition."""

    type: Literal["Periodic"] = "Periodic"


class PECBoundary(BoundaryEdge):
    """Perfect electric conductor boundary condition."""

    type: Literal["PECBoundary"] = "PECBoundary"


class PMCBoundary(BoundaryEdge):
    """Perfect magnetic conductor boundary condition."""

    type: Literal["PMCBoundary"] = "PMCBoundary"


ImplementedBoundaryEdge = Periodic | PECBoundary | PMCBoundary


def boundary_edge_model_from_value(value: object) -> ImplementedBoundaryEdge:
    """Normalize a supported Phase 1 non-absorbing boundary edge."""

    if isinstance(value, (Periodic, PECBoundary, PMCBoundary)):
        return value
    if not isinstance(value, Mapping):
        raise TypeError(f"expected a boundary-edge mapping, got {type(value)!r}")
    boundary_type = str(value.get("type"))
    if boundary_type == "Periodic":
        return Periodic(**value)
    if boundary_type == "PECBoundary":
        return PECBoundary(**value)
    if boundary_type == "PMCBoundary":
        return PMCBoundary(**value)
    raise TypeError(f"unsupported Phase 1 non-absorbing boundary edge type {boundary_type!r}")


class Boundary(TaggedModel):
    """Boundary pair across one simulation axis."""

    type: Literal["Boundary"] = "Boundary"
    plus: object = Field(default_factory=Periodic)
    minus: object = Field(default_factory=Periodic)

    @field_validator("plus", "minus")
    @classmethod
    def _validate_edge(cls, value: object) -> object:
        if isinstance(value, (Periodic, PECBoundary, PMCBoundary)):
            return value
        if isinstance(value, Mapping):
            boundary_type = str(value.get("type"))
            if boundary_type in {"Periodic", "PECBoundary", "PMCBoundary"}:
                return boundary_edge_model_from_value(value)
        return value

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _coerce_periodic_against_conductors(self) -> Boundary:
        plus = self.plus
        minus = self.minus
        changed = False

        if isinstance(minus, (PECBoundary, PMCBoundary)) and isinstance(plus, Periodic):
            plus = minus
            changed = True
        elif isinstance(plus, (PECBoundary, PMCBoundary)) and isinstance(minus, Periodic):
            minus = plus
            changed = True

        if changed:
            import warnings
            from autofdtd.core.validation import AutoFDTDValidationWarning

            warnings.warn(
                "A periodic boundary opposite a PEC/PMC boundary is coerced to the conductor "
                "boundary so runtime halo handling stays reflection-only on that axis.",
                AutoFDTDValidationWarning,
                stacklevel=2,
            )
            object.__setattr__(self, "plus", plus)
            object.__setattr__(self, "minus", minus)

        return self

    def __getitem__(self, field_name: str) -> object:
        if field_name == "plus":
            return self.plus
        if field_name == "minus":
            return self.minus
        if field_name == "type":
            return self.type
        raise KeyError(field_name)

    @classmethod
    def periodic(cls) -> Boundary:
        return cls(plus=Periodic(), minus=Periodic())

    @classmethod
    def pec(cls) -> Boundary:
        return cls(plus=PECBoundary(), minus=PECBoundary())

    @classmethod
    def pmc(cls) -> Boundary:
        return cls(plus=PMCBoundary(), minus=PMCBoundary())


def boundary_model_from_value(value: object) -> Boundary:
    """Normalize a supported axis boundary pair."""

    if isinstance(value, Boundary):
        return value
    if not isinstance(value, Mapping):
        raise TypeError(f"expected a boundary mapping, got {type(value)!r}")
    if "plus" not in value and "minus" not in value:
        edge = boundary_edge_model_from_value(value)
        return Boundary(plus=edge, minus=edge)
    return Boundary(**value)


class BoundarySpec(TaggedModel):
    """Boundary conditions across the x, y, and z simulation axes."""

    type: Literal["BoundarySpec"] = "BoundarySpec"
    x: Boundary = Field(default_factory=Boundary.periodic)
    y: Boundary = Field(default_factory=Boundary.periodic)
    z: Boundary = Field(default_factory=Boundary.periodic)

    @field_validator("x", "y", "z", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _coerce_axis_boundary(cls, value: object) -> object:
        if isinstance(value, (Boundary, Periodic, PECBoundary, PMCBoundary)):
            return value
        if isinstance(value, Mapping):
            boundary_type = str(value.get("type"))
            if boundary_type in {"Boundary", "Periodic", "PECBoundary", "PMCBoundary"}:
                return boundary_model_from_value(value)
        return value

    def __getitem__(self, field_name: str) -> Boundary:
        if field_name == "x":
            return self.x
        if field_name == "y":
            return self.y
        if field_name == "z":
            return self.z
        raise KeyError(field_name)

    def as_tuple(self) -> tuple[Boundary, Boundary, Boundary]:
        return (self.x, self.y, self.z)

    @classmethod
    def all_sides(cls, boundary: ImplementedBoundaryEdge) -> BoundarySpec:
        return cls(
            x=Boundary(plus=boundary, minus=boundary),
            y=Boundary(plus=boundary, minus=boundary),
            z=Boundary(plus=boundary, minus=boundary),
        )

    @classmethod
    def pec(cls, *, x: bool = False, y: bool = False, z: bool = False) -> BoundarySpec:
        return cls(
            x=Boundary.pec() if x else Boundary.periodic(),
            y=Boundary.pec() if y else Boundary.periodic(),
            z=Boundary.pec() if z else Boundary.periodic(),
        )

    @classmethod
    def pmc(cls, *, x: bool = False, y: bool = False, z: bool = False) -> BoundarySpec:
        return cls(
            x=Boundary.pmc() if x else Boundary.periodic(),
            y=Boundary.pmc() if y else Boundary.periodic(),
            z=Boundary.pmc() if z else Boundary.periodic(),
        )

    @classmethod
    def periodic(
        cls, *, x: bool = True, y: bool = True, z: bool = True
    ) -> BoundarySpec:
        return cls(
            x=Boundary.periodic() if x else Boundary.periodic(),
            y=Boundary.periodic() if y else Boundary.periodic(),
            z=Boundary.periodic() if z else Boundary.periodic(),
        )


def boundary_spec_model_from_value(value: object) -> BoundarySpec:
    """Normalize a supported BoundarySpec container."""

+def _reflection_signs_for_axis(
+    symmetry: int,
+    axis_name: Literal["x", "y", "z"],
+) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]:
+    axis_index = "xyz".index(axis_name)

    PMC = "pmc"


class CompiledBoundaryEdge(AutoFDTDModel):
    """Runtime-ready metadata for one boundary face."""

    type: str = "CompiledBoundaryEdge"
    axis: Literal["x", "y", "z"]
    side: Literal["minus", "plus"]
    mode: BoundaryMode
    electric_signs: tuple[int, int, int]
    magnetic_signs: tuple[int, int, int]
    source_side: Literal["minus", "plus"]


class CompiledBoundaryAxis(AutoFDTDModel):
    """Runtime-ready metadata for one axis boundary pair."""

    type: str = "CompiledBoundaryAxis"
    axis: Literal["x", "y", "z"]
    minus: CompiledBoundaryEdge
    plus: CompiledBoundaryEdge
    exchange_kind: Literal["periodic", "reflective"]


class CompiledBoundarySpec(AutoFDTDModel):
    """Compiled boundary metadata consumed by the Phase 1 timestep loop."""

    type: str = "CompiledBoundarySpec"
    x: CompiledBoundaryAxis
    y: CompiledBoundaryAxis
    z: CompiledBoundaryAxis
    periodic_axes: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    reflective_axes: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    halo_depth: int = 1
    stage_order: tuple[str, ...] = ("electric_boundary", "magnetic_boundary")

    def axes(self) -> tuple[CompiledBoundaryAxis, CompiledBoundaryAxis, CompiledBoundaryAxis]:
        return (self.x, self.y, self.z)


def _mode_for_edge(value: object) -> BoundaryMode:
    edge = boundary_edge_model_from_value(value)
    if isinstance(edge, Periodic):
        return BoundaryMode.PERIODIC
    if isinstance(edge, PECBoundary):
        return BoundaryMode.PEC
    if isinstance(edge, PMCBoundary):
        return BoundaryMode.PMC
    raise TypeError(f"unsupported boundary edge type {type(edge)!r}")


def _reflection_signs(
    mode: BoundaryMode, axis: int
) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]:
    normal = [1, 1, 1]
    tangential = [-1, -1, -1]
    normal[axis] = -1
    tangential[axis] = 1
    if mode is BoundaryMode.PEC:
        electric = tuple(tangential)
        magnetic = tuple(normal)
        return electric, magnetic
    if mode is BoundaryMode.PMC:
        electric = tuple(normal)
        magnetic = tuple(tangential)
        return electric, magnetic
    return (1, 1, 1), (1, 1, 1)


def _compile_axis(axis_name: Literal["x", "y", "z"], boundary: Boundary) -> CompiledBoundaryAxis:
    axis_index = "xyz".index(axis_name)
    minus_mode = _mode_for_edge(boundary.minus)
    plus_mode = _mode_for_edge(boundary.plus)
    if minus_mode != plus_mode and BoundaryMode.PERIODIC in {minus_mode, plus_mode}:
        raise ValueError(
            f"axis {axis_name!r} mixes periodic and reflective boundaries after normalization; "
            "coerce the axis to a single mode before runtime compilation"
        )
    minus_electric_signs, minus_magnetic_signs = _reflection_signs(minus_mode, axis_index)
    plus_electric_signs, plus_magnetic_signs = _reflection_signs(plus_mode, axis_index)
    exchange_kind: Literal["periodic", "reflective"] = (
        "periodic"
        if minus_mode is BoundaryMode.PERIODIC and plus_mode is BoundaryMode.PERIODIC
        else "reflective"
    )
    return CompiledBoundaryAxis(
        axis=axis_name,
        minus=CompiledBoundaryEdge(
            axis=axis_name,
            side="minus",
            mode=minus_mode,
            electric_signs=minus_electric_signs,
            magnetic_signs=minus_magnetic_signs,
            source_side="plus",
        ),
        plus=CompiledBoundaryEdge(
            axis=axis_name,
            side="plus",
            mode=plus_mode,
            electric_signs=plus_electric_signs,
            magnetic_signs=plus_magnetic_signs,
            source_side="minus",
        ),
        exchange_kind=exchange_kind,
    )


def compile_boundary_spec(value: object | None) -> CompiledBoundarySpec:
    """Compile the supported non-absorbing boundary subset into runtime metadata."""

    if value is None:
        boundary_spec = BoundarySpec()
    else:
        try:
            boundary_spec = boundary_spec_model_from_value(value)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            raise ValueError(
                "Phase 1 runtime boundary compilation currently supports only BoundarySpec with "
                "Periodic, PECBoundary, and PMCBoundary entries"
            ) from exc

    compiled_axes = {
        axis_name: _compile_axis(axis_name, axis_boundary)
        for axis_name, axis_boundary in zip("xyz", boundary_spec.as_tuple(), strict=True)
    }
    periodic_axes = tuple(
        axis.axis for axis in compiled_axes.values() if axis.exchange_kind == "periodic"
    )
    reflective_axes = tuple(
        axis.axis for axis in compiled_axes.values() if axis.exchange_kind == "reflective"
    )
    return CompiledBoundarySpec(
        x=compiled_axes["x"],
        y=compiled_axes["y"],
        z=compiled_axes["z"],
        periodic_axes=periodic_axes,
        reflective_axes=reflective_axes,
    )


def normalize_axis_boundary(value: object) -> Boundary:
    """Normalize a single axis boundary using the supported subset."""

    return boundary_model_from_value(value)

+def _phase_factor_for_edge(edge: object, *, side: Literal["minus", "plus"]) -> complex:

+def _symmetry_signs(

+def boundary_edge_transform(
+    values: np.ndarray,
+    edge: CompiledBoundaryEdge,
+    *,
+    field_family: str,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Apply the runtime transform associated with one boundary edge."""
+

+        return np.array(values, copy=True)

+def _phase_factor_for_edge(edge: object, *, side: Literal["minus", "plus"]) -> complex:
+    normalized = boundary_edge_model_from_value(edge)
+    if not isinstance(normalized, BlochBoundary):

+def _symmetry_signs(
+    symmetry: int,
+    axis: int,
+) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]:
+    if symmetry not in (-1, 1):
+        raise ValueError("symmetry metadata only exists for active axes")
+    spatial = [1, 1, 1]
+    pseudo = [-1, -1, -1]
+    spatial[axis] = -1
+    pseudo[axis] = 1
+    electric = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in spatial)
+    magnetic = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in pseudo)
+    return electric, magnetic

+def _phase_factor_for_edge(edge: object, *, side: Literal["minus", "plus"]) -> complex:
+    normalized = boundary_edge_model_from_value(edge)
+    if not isinstance(normalized, BlochBoundary):

+def _symmetry_signs(
+    symmetry: int,
+    axis: int,
+) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]:
+    if symmetry not in (-1, 1):
+        raise ValueError("symmetry metadata only exists for active axes")
+    spatial = [1, 1, 1]
+    pseudo = [-1, -1, -1]
+    spatial[axis] = -1
+    pseudo[axis] = 1
+    electric = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in spatial)
+    magnetic = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in pseudo)
+    return electric, magnetic

+class BlochBoundary(BoundaryEdge):

+def _phase_factor_for_edge(edge: object, *, side: Literal["minus", "plus"]) -> complex:
+    normalized = boundary_edge_model_from_value(edge)
+    if not isinstance(normalized, BlochBoundary):
+        return 1.0 + 0.0j
+    phase = normalized.bloch_phase
+    return phase.conjugate() if side == "minus" else phase

+def _symmetry_signs(
+    symmetry: int,
+    axis: int,
+) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]:
+    if symmetry not in (-1, 1):
+        raise ValueError("symmetry metadata only exists for active axes")
+    spatial = [1, 1, 1]
+    pseudo = [-1, -1, -1]
+    spatial[axis] = -1
+    pseudo[axis] = 1
+    electric = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in spatial)
+    magnetic = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in pseudo)
+    return electric, magnetic

+def _phase_factor_for_edge(edge: object, *, side: Literal["minus", "plus"]) -> complex:

+def _reflection_signs_for_axis(
+    symmetry: int,
+    axis_name: Literal["x", "y", "z"],
+) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]:
+    axis_index = "xyz".index(axis_name)
+    spatial_reflection = [1, 1, 1]
+    pseudo_reflection = [-1, -1, -1]
+    spatial_reflection[axis_index] = -1
+    pseudo_reflection[axis_index] = 1
+    electric = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in spatial_reflection)
+    magnetic = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in pseudo_reflection)
+    return electric, magnetic
+
+
+def _symmetry_axes_to_ir(symmetry: tuple[int, int, int]) -> tuple[SymmetryAxisIR, ...]:
+    axes: list[SymmetryAxisIR] = []
+    for axis_name, axis_value in zip("xyz", symmetry, strict=True):
+        if axis_value == 0:

+                electric_signs=electric_signs,
+                magnetic_signs=magnetic_signs,
+            )
+        )
+    return tuple(axes)

+def boundary_edge_transform(
+    values: np.ndarray,
+    edge: CompiledBoundaryEdge,
+    *,
+    field_family: str,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Apply the runtime transform associated with one boundary edge."""
+
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.PERIODIC:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True)
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.BLOCH:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True) * values.dtype.type(edge.phase_factor)
+    signs_name = "electric_signs" if field_family == "electric" else "magnetic_signs"
+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(edge, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)
+
+

+    """Apply mirror-symmetry signs to vector values imported from a reflected chunk."""
+
+    signs_name = "electric_signs" if field_family == "electric" else "magnetic_signs"
+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(symmetry_axis, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)

+def _phase_factor_for_edge(edge: object, *, side: Literal["minus", "plus"]) -> complex:

+def boundary_edge_transform(

+    *,

+    """Apply the runtime transform associated with one boundary edge."""

+def _phase_factor_for_edge(edge: object, *, side: Literal["minus", "plus"]) -> complex:

-def boundary_spec_to_ir(value: object) -> BoundarySpecIR | ComponentIR:
+def _reflection_signs_for_axis(
+    symmetry: int,
+    axis_name: Literal["x", "y", "z"],
+) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]:
+    axis_index = "xyz".index(axis_name)
+    spatial_reflection = [1, 1, 1]
+    pseudo_reflection = [-1, -1, -1]
+    spatial_reflection[axis_index] = -1
+    pseudo_reflection[axis_index] = 1
+    electric = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in spatial_reflection)
+    magnetic = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in pseudo_reflection)
+    return electric, magnetic
+
+
+def _symmetry_axes_to_ir(symmetry: tuple[int, int, int]) -> tuple[SymmetryAxisIR, ...]:
+    axes: list[SymmetryAxisIR] = []
+    for axis_name, axis_value in zip("xyz", symmetry, strict=True):
+        if axis_value == 0:
+            continue
+        electric_signs, magnetic_signs = _reflection_signs_for_axis(axis_value, axis_name)
+        axes.append(
+            SymmetryAxisIR(
+                axis=axis_name,
+                symmetry=axis_value,
+                electric_signs=electric_signs,
+                magnetic_signs=magnetic_signs,
+            )
+        )
+    return tuple(axes)
+

+def boundary_edge_transform(
+    values: np.ndarray,
+    edge: CompiledBoundaryEdge,
+    *,
+    field_family: str,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Apply the runtime transform associated with one boundary edge."""
+
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.PERIODIC:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True)
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.BLOCH:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True) * values.dtype.type(edge.phase_factor)
+    signs_name = "electric_signs" if field_family == "electric" else "magnetic_signs"
+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(edge, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)
+
+
+def symmetry_transform(
+    values: np.ndarray,
+    symmetry_axis: CompiledSymmetryAxis,
+    *,
+    field_family: str,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Apply mirror-symmetry signs to vector values imported from a reflected chunk."""
+
+    signs_name = "electric_signs" if field_family == "electric" else "magnetic_signs"
+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(symmetry_axis, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)

+def boundary_edge_transform(
+    values: np.ndarray,
+    edge: CompiledBoundaryEdge,
+    *,
+    field_family: str,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Apply the runtime transform associated with one boundary edge."""
+
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.PERIODIC:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True)
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.BLOCH:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True) * values.dtype.type(edge.phase_factor)
+    signs_name = "electric_signs" if field_family == "electric" else "magnetic_signs"
+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(edge, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)
+
+

+
+    signs_name = "electric_signs" if field_family == "electric" else "magnetic_signs"
+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(symmetry_axis, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)

+def _reflection_signs_for_axis(
+    symmetry: int,
+    axis_name: Literal["x", "y", "z"],
+) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]:
+    axis_index = "xyz".index(axis_name)
+    spatial_reflection = [1, 1, 1]
+    pseudo_reflection = [-1, -1, -1]
+    spatial_reflection[axis_index] = -1
+    pseudo_reflection[axis_index] = 1
+    electric = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in spatial_reflection)
+    magnetic = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in pseudo_reflection)
+    return electric, magnetic
+
+
+def _symmetry_axes_to_ir(symmetry: tuple[int, int, int]) -> tuple[SymmetryAxisIR, ...]:
+    axes: list[SymmetryAxisIR] = []
+    for axis_name, axis_value in zip("xyz", symmetry, strict=True):
+        if axis_value == 0:
+            continue
+        electric_signs, magnetic_signs = _reflection_signs_for_axis(axis_value, axis_name)
+        axes.append(
+            SymmetryAxisIR(
+                axis=axis_name,
+                symmetry=axis_value,
+                electric_signs=electric_signs,
+                magnetic_signs=magnetic_signs,
+            )
+        )
+    return tuple(axes)
+

+def boundary_edge_transform(
+    values: np.ndarray,
+    edge: CompiledBoundaryEdge,
+    *,
+    field_family: str,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Apply the runtime transform associated with one boundary edge."""
+
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.PERIODIC:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True)
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.BLOCH:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True) * values.dtype.type(edge.phase_factor)
+    signs_name = "electric_signs" if field_family == "electric" else "magnetic_signs"
+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(edge, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)
+
+
+def symmetry_transform(

+    *,

+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Apply mirror-symmetry signs to vector values imported from a reflected chunk."""
+
+    signs_name = "electric_signs" if field_family == "electric" else "magnetic_signs"
+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(symmetry_axis, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)

+def _reflection_signs_for_axis(

+def boundary_edge_transform(
+    values: np.ndarray,
+    edge: CompiledBoundaryEdge,
+    *,
+    field_family: str,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Apply the runtime transform associated with one boundary edge."""
+
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.PERIODIC:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True)
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.BLOCH:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True) * values.dtype.type(edge.phase_factor)
+    signs_name = "electric_signs" if field_family == "electric" else "magnetic_signs"
+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(edge, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)
+
+
+def symmetry_transform(
+    values: np.ndarray,

+    *,
+    field_family: str,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Apply mirror-symmetry signs to vector values imported from a reflected chunk."""
+
+    signs_name = "electric_signs" if field_family == "electric" else "magnetic_signs"
+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(symmetry_axis, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)

+def boundary_edge_to_ir(value: object) -> BoundaryEdgeIR:
+    """Lower a supported boundary edge into typed execution IR."""
+

+        return PMCBoundaryIR(name=edge.name)
+    return component_to_ir(value, family=ComponentFamily.BOUNDARY)

+def boundary_to_ir(value: object) -> BoundaryIR | ComponentIR:
+    """Lower a supported axis boundary pair into typed execution IR."""
+
+    boundary: Boundary | None = None
+    if isinstance(value, Boundary):
+        boundary = value
+    elif isinstance(value, Mapping) and str(value.get("type")) in {
+        "Boundary",
+        "Periodic",
+        "BlochBoundary",
+        "PECBoundary",
+        "PMCBoundary",
+    }:
+        boundary = boundary_model_from_value(value)
+    if boundary is None:
+        return component_to_ir(value, family=ComponentFamily.BOUNDARY)
+    return BoundaryIR(
+        plus=boundary_edge_to_ir(boundary.plus),
+        minus=boundary_edge_to_ir(boundary.minus),
+    )

+def _reflection_signs_for_axis(
+    symmetry: int,
+    axis_name: Literal["x", "y", "z"],
+) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]:
+    axis_index = "xyz".index(axis_name)
+    spatial_reflection = [1, 1, 1]
+    pseudo_reflection = [-1, -1, -1]
+    spatial_reflection[axis_index] = -1
+    pseudo_reflection[axis_index] = 1
+    electric = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in spatial_reflection)
+    magnetic = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in pseudo_reflection)
+    return electric, magnetic
+
+
+def _symmetry_axes_to_ir(symmetry: tuple[int, int, int]) -> tuple[SymmetryAxisIR, ...]:
+    axes: list[SymmetryAxisIR] = []
+    for axis_name, axis_value in zip("xyz", symmetry, strict=True):
+        if axis_value == 0:
+            continue
+        electric_signs, magnetic_signs = _reflection_signs_for_axis(axis_value, axis_name)
+        axes.append(
+            SymmetryAxisIR(
+                axis=axis_name,
+                symmetry=axis_value,
+                electric_signs=electric_signs,
+                magnetic_signs=magnetic_signs,
+            )
+        )
+    return tuple(axes)
+

"""Boundary compilation helpers for the foundational non-absorbing Phase 1 surface."""

from __future__ import annotations

import cmath
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Literal

from autofdtd.boundaries import (
    BlochBoundary,
    Boundary,
    BoundarySpec,
    PECBoundary,
    PMCBoundary,
    Periodic,
    boundary_edge_model_from_value,
    boundary_model_from_value,
    boundary_spec_model_from_value,
)
from autofdtd.core.models import AutoFDTDModel


class BoundaryMode(StrEnum):
    """Runtime boundary mode consumed by staged halo handling."""

    PERIODIC = "periodic"
    BLOCH = "bloch"
    PEC = "pec"
    PMC = "pmc"


class CompiledBoundaryEdge(AutoFDTDModel):
    """Runtime-ready metadata for one boundary face."""

    type: str = "CompiledBoundaryEdge"
    axis: Literal["x", "y", "z"]
    side: Literal["minus", "plus"]
    mode: BoundaryMode
    electric_signs: tuple[int, int, int]
    magnetic_signs: tuple[int, int, int]
    source_side: Literal["minus", "plus"]
    phase_factor: complex = 1.0 + 0.0j


class CompiledBoundaryAxis(AutoFDTDModel):
    """Runtime-ready metadata for one axis boundary pair."""

    type: str = "CompiledBoundaryAxis"
    axis: Literal["x", "y", "z"]
    minus: CompiledBoundaryEdge
    plus: CompiledBoundaryEdge
    exchange_kind: Literal["periodic", "bloch", "reflective"]


class CompiledSymmetryAxis(AutoFDTDModel):
    """Reflection-sign metadata for one reduced symmetry axis."""

    type: str = "CompiledSymmetryAxis"
    axis: Literal["x", "y", "z"]
    symmetry: Literal[-1, 1]
    electric_signs: tuple[int, int, int]
    magnetic_signs: tuple[int, int, int]


class CompiledBoundarySpec(AutoFDTDModel):
    """Compiled boundary metadata consumed by the Phase 1 timestep loop."""

    type: str = "CompiledBoundarySpec"
    x: CompiledBoundaryAxis
    y: CompiledBoundaryAxis
    z: CompiledBoundaryAxis
    periodic_axes: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    bloch_axes: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    reflective_axes: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    requires_complex_fields: bool = False
    symmetry: tuple[int, int, int] = (0, 0, 0)
    active_symmetry_axes: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    symmetry_axes: tuple[CompiledSymmetryAxis, ...] = ()
    halo_depth: int = 1
    stage_order: tuple[str, ...] = ("electric_boundary", "magnetic_boundary")

    def axes(self) -> tuple[CompiledBoundaryAxis, CompiledBoundaryAxis, CompiledBoundaryAxis]:
        return (self.x, self.y, self.z)


def _mode_for_edge(value: object) -> BoundaryMode:
    edge = boundary_edge_model_from_value(value)
    if isinstance(edge, Periodic):
        return BoundaryMode.PERIODIC
    if isinstance(edge, BlochBoundary):
        return BoundaryMode.BLOCH
    if isinstance(edge, PECBoundary):
        return BoundaryMode.PEC
    if isinstance(edge, PMCBoundary):
        return BoundaryMode.PMC
    raise TypeError(f"unsupported boundary edge type {type(edge)!r}")


def _reflection_signs(
    mode: BoundaryMode, axis: int
) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]:
    normal = [1, 1, 1]
    tangential = [-1, -1, -1]
    normal[axis] = -1
    tangential[axis] = 1
    if mode is BoundaryMode.PEC:
        electric = tuple(tangential)
        magnetic = tuple(normal)
        return electric, magnetic
    if mode is BoundaryMode.PMC:
        electric = tuple(normal)
        magnetic = tuple(tangential)
        return electric, magnetic
    return (1, 1, 1), (1, 1, 1)


def _phase_factor_for_edge(edge: object, *, side: Literal["minus", "plus"]) -> complex:
    normalized = boundary_edge_model_from_value(edge)
    if not isinstance(normalized, BlochBoundary):
        return 1.0 + 0.0j
    phase = normalized.bloch_phase
    return phase.conjugate() if side == "minus" else phase


def _symmetry_signs(
    symmetry: int,
    axis: int,
) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]:
    if symmetry not in (-1, 1):
        raise ValueError("symmetry metadata only exists for active axes")
    spatial = [1, 1, 1]
    pseudo = [-1, -1, -1]
    spatial[axis] = -1
    pseudo[axis] = 1
    electric = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in spatial)
    magnetic = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in pseudo)
    return electric, magnetic


def _compile_axis(axis_name: Literal["x", "y", "z"], boundary: Boundary) -> CompiledBoundaryAxis:
    axis_index = "xyz".index(axis_name)
    minus_mode = _mode_for_edge(boundary.minus)
    plus_mode = _mode_for_edge(boundary.plus)
    if minus_mode != plus_mode and {minus_mode, plus_mode} & {
        BoundaryMode.PERIODIC,
        BoundaryMode.BLOCH,
    }:
        raise ValueError(
            f"axis {axis_name!r} mixes periodic-phase and reflective boundaries after normalization; "
            "coerce the axis to a single mode before runtime compilation"
        )
    minus_electric_signs, minus_magnetic_signs = _reflection_signs(minus_mode, axis_index)
    plus_electric_signs, plus_magnetic_signs = _reflection_signs(plus_mode, axis_index)
    if minus_mode is BoundaryMode.PERIODIC and plus_mode is BoundaryMode.PERIODIC:
        exchange_kind: Literal["periodic", "bloch", "reflective"] = "periodic"
    elif minus_mode is BoundaryMode.BLOCH and plus_mode is BoundaryMode.BLOCH:
        exchange_kind = "bloch"
    else:
        exchange_kind = "reflective"
    return CompiledBoundaryAxis(
        axis=axis_name,
        minus=CompiledBoundaryEdge(
            axis=axis_name,
            side="minus",
            mode=minus_mode,
            electric_signs=minus_electric_signs,
            magnetic_signs=minus_magnetic_signs,
            source_side="plus",
            phase_factor=_phase_factor_for_edge(boundary.minus, side="minus"),
        ),
        plus=CompiledBoundaryEdge(
            axis=axis_name,
            side="plus",
            mode=plus_mode,
            electric_signs=plus_electric_signs,
            magnetic_signs=plus_magnetic_signs,
            source_side="minus",
            phase_factor=_phase_factor_for_edge(boundary.plus, side="plus"),
        ),
        exchange_kind=exchange_kind,
    )


def _compile_symmetry_axes(
    symmetry: tuple[int, int, int],
) -> tuple[CompiledSymmetryAxis, ...]:
    compiled: list[CompiledSymmetryAxis] = []
    for axis_name, axis_value in zip("xyz", symmetry, strict=True):
        if axis_value == 0:
            continue
        electric_signs, magnetic_signs = _symmetry_signs(axis_value, "xyz".index(axis_name))
        compiled.append(
            CompiledSymmetryAxis(
                axis=axis_name,
                symmetry=axis_value,
                electric_signs=electric_signs,
                magnetic_signs=magnetic_signs,
            )
        )
    return tuple(compiled)


def compile_boundary_spec(
    value: object | None,
    *,
    symmetry: tuple[int, int, int] = (0, 0, 0),
) -> CompiledBoundarySpec:
    """Compile the supported non-absorbing boundary subset into runtime metadata."""

    if value is None:
        boundary_spec = BoundarySpec()
    else:
        try:
            boundary_spec = boundary_spec_model_from_value(value)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            raise ValueError(
                "Phase 1 runtime boundary compilation currently supports only BoundarySpec with "
                "Periodic, BlochBoundary, PECBoundary, and PMCBoundary entries"
            ) from exc

    compiled_axes = {
        axis_name: _compile_axis(axis_name, axis_boundary)
        for axis_name, axis_boundary in zip("xyz", boundary_spec.as_tuple(), strict=True)
    }
    periodic_axes = tuple(
        axis.axis for axis in compiled_axes.values() if axis.exchange_kind == "periodic"
    )
    bloch_axes = tuple(axis.axis for axis in compiled_axes.values() if axis.exchange_kind == "bloch")
    reflective_axes = tuple(
        axis.axis for axis in compiled_axes.values() if axis.exchange_kind == "reflective"
    )
    symmetry_axes = _compile_symmetry_axes(symmetry)
    return CompiledBoundarySpec(
        x=compiled_axes["x"],
        y=compiled_axes["y"],
        z=compiled_axes["z"],
        periodic_axes=periodic_axes,
        bloch_axes=bloch_axes,
        reflective_axes=reflective_axes,
        requires_complex_fields=bool(bloch_axes),
        symmetry=symmetry,
        active_symmetry_axes=tuple(axis.axis for axis in symmetry_axes),
        symmetry_axes=symmetry_axes,
    )


def normalize_axis_boundary(value: object) -> Boundary:
    """Normalize a single axis boundary using the supported subset."""

    return boundary_model_from_value(value)

def test_boundary_coerces_periodic_opposite_conductor_with_warning() -> None:
    with pytest.warns(
        AutoFDTDValidationWarning,
        match="periodic boundary opposite a PEC/PMC boundary",
    ):
        boundary = Boundary(minus=PECBoundary(), plus=Periodic())

    assert boundary.minus.type == "PECBoundary"
    assert boundary.plus.type == "PECBoundary"


def test_simulation_normalizes_supported_boundary_subset() -> None:
    simulation = Simulation(
        size=(1.0, 1.0, 1.0),
        run_time=1.0,
        boundary_spec={
            "type": "BoundarySpec",
            "x": {"type": "Periodic"},
            "y": {
                "type": "Boundary",
                "minus": {"type": "PECBoundary"},
                "plus": {"type": "Periodic"},
            },
            "z": {"type": "PMCBoundary"},
        },
    )

    assert simulation.boundary_spec["x"]["minus"]["type"] == "Periodic"
    assert simulation.boundary_spec["x"]["plus"]["type"] == "Periodic"
    assert simulation.boundary_spec["y"]["minus"]["type"] == "PECBoundary"
    assert simulation.boundary_spec["y"]["plus"]["type"] == "PECBoundary"
    assert simulation.boundary_spec["z"]["minus"]["type"] == "PMCBoundary"
    assert simulation.boundary_spec["z"]["plus"]["type"] == "PMCBoundary"

def test_boundary_kernels_apply_periodic_and_reflective_ghost_updates() -> None:
    compiled = compile_boundary_spec(
        BoundarySpec(x=Boundary.bloch(0.25), y=Boundary.pec(), z=Boundary.pmc())
    )
    electric = np.zeros((4, 4, 4, 3), dtype=np.complex128)
    magnetic = np.zeros((4, 4, 4, 3), dtype=np.complex128)

    electric[1, 1, 1] = (1.0, 2.0, 3.0)
    electric[-2, 1, 1] = (4.0, 5.0, 6.0)
    electric[2, 1, 2] = (7.0, 8.0, 9.0)
    electric[1, -2, 2] = (11.0, 12.0, 13.0)
    electric[2, 2, 1] = (14.0, 15.0, 16.0)
    electric[1, 2, -2] = (17.0, 18.0, 19.0)

    magnetic[1, 1, 1] = (21.0, 22.0, 23.0)
    magnetic[-2, 1, 1] = (24.0, 25.0, 26.0)
    magnetic[2, 1, 2] = (27.0, 28.0, 29.0)
    magnetic[2, -2, 2] = (31.0, 32.0, 33.0)
    magnetic[2, 2, 1] = (34.0, 35.0, 36.0)
    magnetic[2, 2, -2] = (37.0, 38.0, 39.0)

    updated_electric, updated_magnetic = apply_boundary_ghosts(electric, magnetic, compiled)

    assert tuple(updated_electric[0, 1, 1]) == pytest.approx((-4.0j, -5.0j, -6.0j))
    assert tuple(updated_electric[-1, 1, 1]) == pytest.approx((1.0j, 2.0j, 3.0j))
    assert tuple(updated_magnetic[0, 1, 1]) == pytest.approx((-24.0j, -25.0j, -26.0j))
    assert tuple(updated_electric[2, 0, 2]) == pytest.approx((-7.0, 8.0, -9.0))
    assert tuple(updated_magnetic[2, 0, 2]) == pytest.approx((27.0, -28.0, 29.0))
    assert tuple(updated_electric[2, 2, 0]) == pytest.approx((14.0, 15.0, -16.0))
    assert tuple(updated_magnetic[2, 2, -1]) == pytest.approx((-37.0, -38.0, 39.0))


def test_boundary_runtime_wrapper_and_ir_lowering_expose_typed_metadata() -> None:
    boundary_spec = BoundarySpec(x=Boundary.bloch(0.25), y=Boundary.pec(), z=Boundary.pmc())

def test_boundary_runtime_exposes_phase_and_symmetry_transforms() -> None:
    runtime = build_boundary_runtime(BoundarySpec(x=Boundary.bloch(0.25)), symmetry=(1, 0, 0))
    vector = np.asarray([[1.0 + 0.0j, 2.0 + 0.0j, 3.0 + 0.0j]], dtype=np.complex128)

    boundary_values = runtime.transform_boundary_values(
        vector,
        runtime.compiled.x.plus,
        field_family="electric",
    )
    mirrored = runtime.transform_symmetry_values(
        vector,
        runtime.compiled.symmetry_axes[0],
        field_family="magnetic",
    )

    assert tuple(boundary_values[0]) == pytest.approx((1.0j, 2.0j, 3.0j))
    assert tuple(mirrored[0]) == pytest.approx((1.0, -2.0, -3.0))
    assert tuple(
        boundary_edge_transform(vector, runtime.compiled.x.minus, field_family="electric")[0]
    ) == pytest.approx((-1.0j, -2.0j, -3.0j))
    assert tuple(symmetry_transform(vector, runtime.compiled.symmetry_axes[0], field_family="electric")[0]) == pytest.approx((-1.0, 2.0, 3.0))


def test_boundary_rejects_single_sided_bloch_and_normalizes_public_api() -> None:

    )

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Bloch boundaries must be applied on both sides"):
        Boundary(minus=BlochBoundary(bloch_vec=0.1), plus=Periodic())

# Phase 1 Maxwell Solver Loop Working Memory

Use this file for cumulative findings, reusable facts, decisions, and cross-task notes.

Keep it concise. Do not repeat information already captured in `loop.prompt.md` or other local files.
Prefer referencing local file paths and distilled takeaways instead of copying long excerpts.

Suggested sections:

- Facts
- Decisions
- Open Questions
- Reusable References
- Task Handoffs

## Facts

- `task-001` starts from an effectively empty repo with no `src/` package or tooling.
- `phase1/feature-checklist.md` is now mirrored in code via `src/autofdtd/planning.py` so later tasks can reuse a local feature/status source instead of reparsing markdown.
- `src/autofdtd/core/containers.py` now holds the first frozen tagged container models for `Structure`, `Scene`, and `Simulation`; `src/autofdtd/api/simulation.py` re-exports them as the public API surface.
- `src/autofdtd/ir/models.py` now defines the first versioned execution IR, with `ComponentIR`, `StructureIR`, `SceneIR`, `SimulationIR`, and `ExecutionPackageIR` as the transport contract.
- `src/autofdtd/core/validation.py` now centralizes Phase 1 normalization rules, unsupported-feature checks, primitive geometry sanity checks, simulation-bound checks, and zero-dimension boundary coercion.
- `src/autofdtd/core/models.py` now provides the shared frozen model contract with `model_tag()`, `copy_update()`, `json_ready()`, and stable JSON serialization helpers reused by both public containers and IR models.
- `src/autofdtd/geometry/primitives.py` now provides typed `Box`, `Sphere`, and `Cylinder` public models plus `GeometryTransform`, bounds, point-containment, and translation helpers.
- `src/autofdtd/ir/models.py` now lowers primitive geometries into typed `BoxIR`, `SphereIR`, and `CylinderIR` payloads with explicit bounds and scene-compilation transform metadata.
- `src/autofdtd/geometry/polyslab.py` now provides a typed `PolySlab` model for simple-polygon extrusions with bounds, containment, translation, and simple-polygon validation; `src/autofdtd/ir/models.py` lowers it into `PolySlabIR`.
- `src/autofdtd/geometry/composite.py` now provides `GeometryGroup`, `Transformed`, `GeometryArray`, and a narrow `ClipOperation` subset (`union`, `intersection`, `difference`) for Phase 1 scene construction.
- `GeometryTransform` now supports explicit rigid-transform composition plus translation, rotation, reflection, and conservative transformed-bounds evaluation for wrapper lowering and scene queries.
- `src/autofdtd/ir/models.py` now carries typed wrapper IR via `GeometryGroupIR`, `TransformedIR`, and `ClipOperationIR`.
- `GeometryArray` uses Tidy3D-style `geometry + offsets + transforms` public semantics, but Phase 1 keeps transforms rigid and linear-only and lowers arrays into explicit grouped instances for IR and overlap evaluation.
- `Scene.structure_precedence()` and `Scene.resolve_structure_stack_at_point()` now expose concrete overlap order with `source_index`, `resolved_priority`, and `precedence_rank`, and `StructureIR` carries the same metadata for later compiler stages.
- `src/autofdtd/grid/specs.py` now provides `AutoGrid`, `GridRefinement`, and `LayerRefinementSpec` in addition to the manual grid models; the current AutoGrid path is wavelength-driven, axis-local, and only applies axis-aligned layer refinement metadata.
- `src/autofdtd/ir/models.py` now lowers `GridSpec` into typed grid IR with per-axis spec payloads, layer-refinement metadata, and resolved boundary and shape metadata, so later compiler work can consume inspectable discretization state instead of reparsing public models.
- `src/autofdtd/grid/subpixel.py` now provides the first explicit subpixel policy layer with `SubpixelSpec`, `Staircasing`, and `PolarizedAveraging`, plus Tidy3D-style `bool` coercion for `Simulation.subpixel`.
- `src/autofdtd/ir/models.py` now lowers subpixel settings into `SubpixelSpecIR` with explicit averaging-vs-staircasing targets and an anisotropic-materialization flag for later scene compilation.
- `src/autofdtd/materials/isotropic.py` now provides typed `Medium`, `PECMedium`, and `PMCMedium` public models with validation and normalization helpers; `src/autofdtd/ir/models.py` lowers them into typed `MediumIR`, `PECMediumIR`, and `PMCMediumIR`.
- `src/autofdtd/compiler/materials.py` now compiles isotropic constitutive coefficients, exposes scene-point medium sampling, and keeps explicit clamp-zero modes for `PECMedium` and `PMCMedium`.
- `src/autofdtd/kernels/materials.py` now provides the first staged constitutive-update helpers with a NumPy path and optional Warp-availability reporting.
- `src/autofdtd/materials/dispersive.py` now provides a Phase 1 `PoleResidue` public model with JSON-safe complex-pair storage, causal validation (`Re(a) <= 0`), `eps_model()`, and limited `Medium` conversion helpers.
- `src/autofdtd/materials/dispersive.py` now also provides a passive homogeneous `Sellmeier` model with `(B_i, C_i)` coefficient storage, direct `eps_model()` evaluation, single-pole `from_dispersion()` fitting, and explicit lowering to an equivalent `PoleResidue` representation.
- `src/autofdtd/materials/dispersive.py` now also provides passive homogeneous `Lorentz`, damped `Drude`, and passive homogeneous `Debye` models with family-specific analytical coefficients and explicit lowering to equivalent `PoleResidue` payloads.
- `src/autofdtd/ir/models.py` now lowers supported dispersive media into typed `PoleResidueIR` payloads instead of a generic medium envelope.
- `src/autofdtd/ir/models.py` now lowers `Sellmeier` into a typed `SellmeierIR` while keeping runtime compilation on the shared pole-residue auxiliary-state contract.
- `src/autofdtd/ir/models.py` now lowers `Lorentz`, `Drude`, and `Debye` into typed IR families while runtime compilation still targets the shared pole-residue auxiliary-state contract.
- `src/autofdtd/compiler/materials.py` now compiles `PoleResidue` media into explicit epsilon-infinity electric coefficients plus per-pole exact-hold recurrence terms for complex auxiliary polarization state.
- `src/autofdtd/compiler/materials.py` now compiles `Sellmeier` by first reducing it to an equivalent `PoleResidue`, then re-tagging the compiled coefficients as `medium_type="Sellmeier"` so scene diagnostics preserve the public family name.
- `src/autofdtd/compiler/materials.py` now compiles `Lorentz`, `Drude`, and `Debye` by first reducing them to equivalent `PoleResidue` terms, re-tagging the compiled coefficients with the public family name, and failing explicitly when converted poles are too stiff for the current exact-hold timestep path.
- `src/autofdtd/kernels/materials.py` now allocates explicit PoleResidue auxiliary state and applies a staged `pole_residue_electric_update()` that subtracts a compiled polarization-current estimate from the baseline electric update.
- `src/autofdtd/materials/anisotropic.py` now provides `AnisotropicMedium` as the implemented diagonal tensor family plus explicit `FullyAnisotropicMedium` and `Medium2D` defer-policy surfaces; `Medium2D` is parseable and convertible to volumetric `AnisotropicMedium`, but direct simulation use stays rejected in Phase 1.
- `src/autofdtd/compiler/materials.py` now compiles `AnisotropicMedium` into `AnisotropicMaterialCoefficients` with one scalar constitutive branch per principal axis, allowing nondispersive, dispersive, and clamp-mode components to coexist without introducing a dense-tensor runtime yet.
- `src/autofdtd/kernels/materials.py` now provides `allocate_anisotropic_state()`, `anisotropic_electric_update()`, and `anisotropic_magnetic_update()` for diagonal tensor updates with per-axis dispersive auxiliary state.
- `src/autofdtd/materials/advanced.py` now maps `LossyMetalMedium`, `PerturbationMedium`, `PerturbationPoleResidue`, `CustomMedium`, and `CustomAnisotropicMedium` into explicit Phase 1 policy surfaces, and `src/autofdtd/core/validation.py` buckets unknown `Custom*` medium tags into the clear custom-media reject path instead of treating them as unmapped types.
- `src/autofdtd/boundaries/models.py` now provides the first typed non-absorbing boundary surface with `Periodic`, `PECBoundary`, `PMCBoundary`, `Boundary`, and `BoundarySpec`, including periodic-opposite-conductor coercion.
- `src/autofdtd/ir/models.py` now lowers the supported boundary subset into typed `PeriodicIR`, `PECBoundaryIR`, `PMCBoundaryIR`, `BoundaryIR`, and `BoundarySpecIR` payloads while leaving unsupported boundary families in the generic boundary envelope.
- `src/autofdtd/compiler/boundaries.py`, `src/autofdtd/kernels/boundaries.py`, and `src/autofdtd/runtime/boundaries.py` now compile the supported subset into explicit halo metadata and apply periodic-copy or conductor-reflection ghost-cell updates for `(nx, ny, nz, 3)` vector fields.

## Decisions

- Reserve subsystem namespaces now: `api`, `core`, `geometry`, `materials`, `boundaries`, `sources`, `monitors`, `grid`, `modes`, `ir`, `compiler`, `runtime`, `kernels`, `diagnostics`, `examples`.
- Use `hatchling` with a `src/` layout and ship a small CLI (`autofdtd-feature-matrix`) so the scaffold has a concrete install/runtime smoke target before solver code exists.
- Keep this task focused on packaging, docs, and planning metadata; full tagged models remain for `task-002` and `task-003`.
- Model ordered overlap explicitly through `Scene.structures_in_resolution_order()`, sorting by resolved priority and then insertion order so later structures still win ties during sequential materialization.
- Keep the initial container layer serialization-light: `to_payload()`, `to_json_text()`, and `write_json()` are enough for snapshots and handoff, while `task-005` can generalize the shared model base.
- Use a generic family-tagged component envelope in the IR so Phase 1 can package realistic simulations before every feature family has concrete typed IR classes; later tasks can specialize payloads without changing bundle shape.
- Bundle packaging is directory-based: `manifest.json` points at a hashed `simulation.json` entrypoint, avoiding self-referential manifest hashing while staying suitable for remote upload or local caching.
- Core validation is checklist-driven: implemented feature tags pass, deferred or rejected tags fail early with explicit errors, and known primitive geometry payloads validate only when enough fields are present so placeholder tagged dicts can survive until their concrete family tasks land.
- Shared model behavior should live in `autofdtd.core.models`; public API and IR classes should subclass it rather than duplicating serialization or copy helpers in subsystem-local base classes.
- Primitive geometry stays axis-aligned in Phase 1 public models; scene-compilation transforms are still explicit so later `Transformed` and grouped-geometry tasks can lower onto the same contract instead of rewriting primitive handling.
- Structure precedence is now inspectable with `Scene.resolve_structure_at_point()`, which mirrors materialization order by applying primitive containment checks in resolved-priority order.
- Keep `GeometryArray` as a public wrapper only; repeated placements lower into ordinary grouped and transformed instances so runtime/compiler code can treat arrays as pre-expanded ordered geometry.
- Phase 1 `PolySlab` scope is intentionally limited to constant-cross-section extrusions of simple polygons on principal axes; non-zero `dilation` or `sidewall_angle`, self-intersections, and curved or boolean polygon features must fail explicitly until later geometry tasks land.
- Keep the feature ledger conservative for clipping: `ClipOperation` remains a deferred family in `planning.py`, but geometry validation explicitly allows the implemented subset and rejects unsupported boolean ops with clear errors.
- Phase 1 transform wrappers are rigid only; free-form affine matrices and exact boolean meshing remain out of scope even though the public model now supports grouped and transformed composition.
- Keep the top-level simulation grid surface strict: `grid_spec` must be a `GridSpec`, `AutoGrid` requires `GridSpec.wavelength`, and `QuasiUniformGrid` remains an explicit deferred error.
- Phase 1 AutoGrid is deliberately narrow: derive a vacuum baseline from wavelength and domain size, discretize piecewise with a simple `max_scale` grading pass, and limit refinement inputs to `LayerRefinementSpec` body and bound hints rather than full geometry-driven meshing.
- Keep Phase 1 subpixel support narrow and explicit: dielectric interfaces may use `PolarizedAveraging` or `Staircasing`, while metal, PEC, PMC, and lossy-metal interfaces stay staircasing-only until anisotropic media and conformal policies land.
- Treat PEC and PMC as explicit constitutive clamp modes in coefficient compilation and runtime helpers instead of pretending they are extremely lossy ordinary media.
- Phase 1 `PoleResidue` keeps complex numbers JSON-safe as `(real, imag)` tuples in the public API and IR so serialization stays stable without inventing ad hoc string encoding.
- Phase 1 PoleResidue runtime support is electric-only and uses one complex polarization accumulator per pole; magnetic dispersion remains out of scope until later material families require it.
- Phase 1 `Sellmeier` support is intentionally passive-only and homogeneous-only: `B_i >= 0`, `C_i >= 0`, zero-`C_i` terms fold into `eps_inf`, and all timestep execution reuses the existing electric-only `PoleResidueMaterialCoefficients` path instead of creating a new auxiliary-state layout.
- Phase 1 `Lorentz` is passive-only (`delta_eps >= 0`, `damping >= 0`, `frequency^2 != damping^2`), `Drude` is limited to damped poles (`damping > 0`) so it can lower cleanly onto the current pole-residue path, and `Debye` is passive-only (`delta_eps >= 0`, `tau > 0`).
- The current exact-hold pole-residue recurrence path can overflow for sufficiently stiff poles relative to `dt`; material compilation now raises an explicit error instead of emitting unusable coefficients, which is especially relevant for very small-`tau` Debye fits.
- Phase 1 anisotropy stops at diagonal tensor media: `AnisotropicMedium` is implemented and IR-lowered, `FullyAnisotropicMedium` remains an explicit deferred error for runtime compilation, and `Medium2D` remains a deferred direct-simulation feature with offline conversion helpers only.
- Advanced material policy is explicit rather than silent: `LossyMetalMedium` and perturbation media are parseable defer buckets with manual fallback helpers, while sampled `Custom*` media are parsed or bucketed only to produce clear reject errors.
- Phase 1 boundary runtime support is intentionally narrow: runtime compilation accepts only `BoundarySpec` composed from `Periodic`, `PECBoundary`, and `PMCBoundary`; PML, Bloch, and ABC-family entries stay parseable at the API layer but are not compiled on this task’s runtime path.
- Conductor boundaries are represented as reflection-sign transforms rather than special-casing them inside the future timestep loop: PEC uses odd tangential electric and odd normal magnetic parity, while PMC uses the opposite parity assignment.

## Task Handoffs

- `task-003` should add versioned IR models under `autofdtd.ir` without coupling them to the public API module layout; it can treat `Simulation.to_payload()` as an interim handoff format, not the final IR contract.
- Later geometry, material, source, and monitor tasks can plug concrete tagged models into the existing container fields without changing the ordered-container semantics.
- `task-004` and `task-005` can reuse `ComponentIR.payload` plus the shared IR schema version constants instead of inventing another transport shape.
- Later geometry, source, monitor, boundary, and grid tasks should route new object models through `autofdtd.core.validation.normalize_component()` or extend its equivalents instead of scattering policy checks across each family.
- Later compiler work can rely on wrapper IR bounds as conservative planning envelopes; exact voxelization or boolean rasterization still belongs in scene compilation rather than the public geometry layer.
- Later compiler work can consume `StructureIR.source_index` plus `StructureIR.precedence_rank` directly when building ordered region materialization plans or conflict diagnostics.
- Later grid/compiler tasks should treat `LayerRefinementSpecIR` as planning metadata only; corner finding, snapping-point localization, and structure-derived meshing still need a separate scene-aware meshing pass.
- Material and compiler tasks should consume `SubpixelSpecIR.averaging_targets` and `requires_anisotropic_materialization` directly instead of re-deriving which interface families need tensor-valued effective media.
- Later runtime and chunk-planning tasks can treat `IsotropicMaterialCoefficients` plus `ConstitutiveMode` as the stable baseline constitutive contract before dispersive and anisotropic state is added.
- Later Lorentz, Drude, Debye, and Sellmeier tasks should lower onto the `PoleResidueMaterialCoefficients` auxiliary-state contract whenever the family can be reduced to pole-residue terms instead of creating parallel runtime state layouts.
- Later subpixel materialization work can target `AnisotropicMaterialCoefficients` plus the diagonal anisotropic kernel path instead of inventing a separate tensor-material runtime for effective-media smoothing.
- Later Bloch and absorbing-boundary tasks should extend `CompiledBoundarySpec` and the boundary ghost-update stage rather than reworking the public `Boundary` or `BoundarySpec` container semantics.

+def boundary_edge_transform(
+    values: np.ndarray,
+    edge: CompiledBoundaryEdge,
+    *,
+    field_family: str,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Apply the runtime transform associated with one boundary edge."""
+
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.PERIODIC:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True)
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.BLOCH:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True) * values.dtype.type(edge.phase_factor)
+    signs_name = "electric_signs" if field_family == "electric" else "magnetic_signs"
+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(edge, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)
+

+def _phase_factor_for_edge(edge: object, *, side: Literal["minus", "plus"]) -> complex:
+    normalized = boundary_edge_model_from_value(edge)
+    if not isinstance(normalized, BlochBoundary):

+def _symmetry_signs(

+    axis: int,
+) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]:
+    if symmetry not in (-1, 1):
+        raise ValueError("symmetry metadata only exists for active axes")
+    spatial = [1, 1, 1]

+    magnetic = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in pseudo)
+    return electric, magnetic

+def boundary_edge_transform(
+    values: np.ndarray,
+    edge: CompiledBoundaryEdge,
+    *,
+    field_family: str,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Apply the runtime transform associated with one boundary edge."""
+
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.PERIODIC:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True)
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.BLOCH:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True) * values.dtype.type(edge.phase_factor)

+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(edge, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)

+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(symmetry_axis, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)

+def _phase_factor_for_edge(edge: object, *, side: Literal["minus", "plus"]) -> complex:
+    normalized = boundary_edge_model_from_value(edge)
+    if not isinstance(normalized, BlochBoundary):
+        return 1.0 + 0.0j
+    phase = normalized.bloch_phase
+    return phase.conjugate() if side == "minus" else phase

+def _symmetry_signs(
+    symmetry: int,
+    axis: int,
+) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]:
+    if symmetry not in (-1, 1):
+        raise ValueError("symmetry metadata only exists for active axes")
+    spatial = [1, 1, 1]
+    pseudo = [-1, -1, -1]
+    spatial[axis] = -1
+    pseudo[axis] = 1
+    electric = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in spatial)
+    magnetic = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in pseudo)
+    return electric, magnetic
+

+def boundary_edge_transform(
+    values: np.ndarray,
+    edge: CompiledBoundaryEdge,
+    *,
+    field_family: str,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Apply the runtime transform associated with one boundary edge."""
+

+        return np.array(values, copy=True)

+def _reflection_signs_for_axis(
+    symmetry: int,
+    axis_name: Literal["x", "y", "z"],
+) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]:
+    axis_index = "xyz".index(axis_name)
+    spatial_reflection = [1, 1, 1]
+    pseudo_reflection = [-1, -1, -1]
+    spatial_reflection[axis_index] = -1
+    pseudo_reflection[axis_index] = 1

+    magnetic = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in pseudo_reflection)

+def boundary_edge_transform(
+    values: np.ndarray,
+    edge: CompiledBoundaryEdge,
+    *,
+    field_family: str,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Apply the runtime transform associated with one boundary edge."""
+
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.PERIODIC:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True)
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.BLOCH:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True) * values.dtype.type(edge.phase_factor)
+    signs_name = "electric_signs" if field_family == "electric" else "magnetic_signs"
+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(edge, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)
+

+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(symmetry_axis, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)

+def _phase_factor_for_edge(edge: object, *, side: Literal["minus", "plus"]) -> complex:

+def _reflection_signs_for_axis(
+    symmetry: int,
+    axis_name: Literal["x", "y", "z"],
+) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]:
+    axis_index = "xyz".index(axis_name)
+    spatial_reflection = [1, 1, 1]
+    pseudo_reflection = [-1, -1, -1]
+    spatial_reflection[axis_index] = -1
+    pseudo_reflection[axis_index] = 1
+    electric = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in spatial_reflection)
+    magnetic = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in pseudo_reflection)
+    return electric, magnetic
+

+def _symmetry_axes_to_ir(symmetry: tuple[int, int, int]) -> tuple[SymmetryAxisIR, ...]:

+        )

+def boundary_edge_transform(
+    values: np.ndarray,
+    edge: CompiledBoundaryEdge,
+    *,
+    field_family: str,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Apply the runtime transform associated with one boundary edge."""
+
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.PERIODIC:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True)
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.BLOCH:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True) * values.dtype.type(edge.phase_factor)
+    signs_name = "electric_signs" if field_family == "electric" else "magnetic_signs"
+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(edge, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)
+

+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(symmetry_axis, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)

+    vector = np.asarray([[1.0 + 0.0j, 2.0 + 0.0j, 3.0 + 0.0j]], dtype=np.complex128)
+
+    boundary_values = runtime.transform_boundary_values(
+        vector,
+        runtime.compiled.x.plus,
+        field_family="electric",
+    )
+    mirrored = runtime.transform_symmetry_values(
+        vector,
+        runtime.compiled.symmetry_axes[0],
+        field_family="magnetic",
+    )
+
+    assert tuple(boundary_values[0]) == pytest.approx((1.0j, 2.0j, 3.0j))
+    assert tuple(mirrored[0]) == pytest.approx((1.0, -2.0, -3.0))
+    assert tuple(
+        boundary_edge_transform(vector, runtime.compiled.x.minus, field_family="electric")[0]
+    ) == pytest.approx((-1.0j, -2.0j, -3.0j))
+    assert tuple(
+        symmetry_transform(
+            vector,
+            runtime.compiled.symmetry_axes[0],
+            field_family="electric",
+        )[0]
+    ) == pytest.approx((-1.0, 2.0, 3.0))
+

+def test_boundary_rejects_single_sided_bloch_and_normalizes_public_api() -> None:
+    boundary = Boundary.bloch(0.125)
+    assert isinstance(boundary.plus, BlochBoundary)
+    assert boundary.plus.bloch_phase == pytest.approx(
+        np.exp(1j * 2.0 * np.pi * 0.125),
+    )
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Bloch boundaries must be applied on both sides"):
+        Boundary(minus=BlochBoundary(bloch_vec=0.1), plus=Periodic())

+def _reflection_signs_for_axis(

+    axis_index = "xyz".index(axis_name)

+def boundary_edge_transform(
+    values: np.ndarray,
+    edge: CompiledBoundaryEdge,
+    *,
+    field_family: str,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Apply the runtime transform associated with one boundary edge."""

+        return np.array(values, copy=True)

+def _phase_factor_for_edge(edge: object, *, side: Literal["minus", "plus"]) -> complex:
+    normalized = boundary_edge_model_from_value(edge)
+    if not isinstance(normalized, BlochBoundary):
+        return 1.0 + 0.0j
+    phase = normalized.bloch_phase
+    return phase.conjugate() if side == "minus" else phase

+def _symmetry_signs(
+    symmetry: int,
+    axis: int,
+) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]:
+    if symmetry not in (-1, 1):
+        raise ValueError("symmetry metadata only exists for active axes")
+    spatial = [1, 1, 1]
+    pseudo = [-1, -1, -1]
+    spatial[axis] = -1
+    pseudo[axis] = 1
+    electric = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in spatial)
+    magnetic = tuple(sign * symmetry for sign in pseudo)
+    return electric, magnetic

+def boundary_edge_transform(
+    values: np.ndarray,
+    edge: CompiledBoundaryEdge,
+    *,
+    field_family: str,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Apply the runtime transform associated with one boundary edge."""
+
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.PERIODIC:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True)
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.BLOCH:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True) * values.dtype.type(edge.phase_factor)
+    signs_name = "electric_signs" if field_family == "electric" else "magnetic_signs"
+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(edge, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)
+

+def _phase_factor_for_edge(edge: object, *, side: Literal["minus", "plus"]) -> complex:

+def boundary_edge_transform(
+    values: np.ndarray,
+    edge: CompiledBoundaryEdge,
+    *,
+    field_family: str,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Apply the runtime transform associated with one boundary edge."""
+
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.PERIODIC:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True)
+    if edge.mode is BoundaryMode.BLOCH:
+        return np.array(values, copy=True) * values.dtype.type(edge.phase_factor)
+    signs_name = "electric_signs" if field_family == "electric" else "magnetic_signs"
+    return np.array(values, copy=True) * np.asarray(getattr(edge, signs_name), dtype=values.dtype)
+
+
+def symmetry_transform(
+    values: np.ndarray,
+    symmetry_axis: CompiledSymmetryAxis,
+    *,
+    field_family: str,
+) -> np.ndarray:
